authorRole: Independent public infrastructure expectation designer; author of earlier trusted boundary/stream tests, not a distinct authenticated GitHub reviewer.

parentDesign.readScope: Only that design and previously inspected committed public source; no private holdout, raw server-reference manifest or ignored historical capture reads.

scope.purpose: Freeze literal trusted-fixture proxy/topology counterexamples before infrastructure implementation. No Next app, real browser, real Postgres, provider, production or product acceptance assertion is added by this inventory.

fixedIdentities.identityLimit: These public literal IDs are correlation labels for controlled fixtures, not credentials, actor authorization, action authenticity or production provenance.

trustRules: All peers/controllers/observers in this inventory are separately owned trusted literal fixture programs; none loads candidate code or expected product values into an app sandbox.
Native kernel/socket/process/configuration observations and independently read bytes are required; a fixture saying PASS is never sufficient.
Private management handshake ordinals bind cross-process causal acknowledgments. Wall clocks are diagnostic only; no comparison of unrelated process counters supplies a missing edge.
Preserve Host/Origin/forwarded-origin bytes without silently repairing Next CSRF. Real Next behavior remains unknown.
Never drain/complete/replace a response merely to make EOF. Canceled and missing browser terminals remain strict v1 blockers in future product runs.
Actual network restrictions require directional policy plus inspected native configuration and live-target negative controls. --internal and network membership are insufficient.

bounds.reviewedEnvelopeLimit: These are the current static-source limits, not measured multi-container/native Next capacity. This inventory does not authorize their change or certify that the proposed topology fits them.
bounds.newBoundsReviewStatus: Prospectively frozen proposals, NOT measured or already approved. Root/security review is required before execution. They deliberately describe only small literal fixtures; no full Next build/native capacity is invented.
bounds.overflowPolicy: Block on any bound violation; retain actual available raw bytes with explicit incomplete/overflow flags. Finite overflow fixtures fit the larger raw artifact budget. Arbitrarily unbounded output must be stopped and cannot be described as fully retained.

literalBytePolicy.encoding: hex fields define exact bytes; textual HTTP uses exact ASCII plus CRLF. Digests bind complete fixture bytes. No trimming/normalizing/UTF-8 replacement is permitted.
literalBytePolicy.privacy: These public synthetic request/response byte fixtures intentionally contain no auth headers, cookies, credentials or personal data, so exact raw wire retention is safe. This is NOT permission to retain real product request bodies/headers, session state or raw server-reference manifests.
literalBytePolicy.framing: Exact raw HTTP/1.1 forwarding is frozen here. Deliberate protocol translation, hop-header mutation or rechunking would need a separate prospective design; do not weaken an exact-wire comparison after output is seen.

cases.reason: Proves the allowed browser-to-proxy-to-app path is live rather than treating absent services as isolation.

literalStimulus.request:
GET /literal/ping HTTP/1.1
Host: board.fixture.invalid:8080
Connection: close

requiredActualObservations: Actual client connection succeeds only through the intermediary. Literal app receives the exact request bytes once and client receives the exact frozen response bytes once.
Retain actual network/container configuration and separate per-socket send/receive ordinals; producer log text alone is insufficient.

cases.reason: Every private endpoint needs a live authorized control so denied probes are not explained by a stopped listener.
requiredActualObservations: Each exact authorized exchange succeeds before and after the corresponding denied probes.
DB and CDP endpoints in this inventory are literal TCP stand-ins. This does not prove Postgres privileges, real auth or browser/CDP compatibility.

cases.reason: An internal network flag alone does not establish app egress restrictions.
requiredActualObservations: Actual attempted sockets fail or reach a finite blocked deadline according to the frozen packet policy; no canary receives the literal APP-DENY-01 payload.
Every target is an owned live canary, not a real external service. Native allow/deny policy and canary inventories are retained. No secret is transmitted.

cases.reason: Browser/client must not bypass the intermediary or reach DB/observer/control interfaces.
requiredActualObservations: All actual denied connection attempts have native socket outcomes; live canaries receive no payload.
NET01 still succeeds, distinguishing intended restrictions from loss of all networking.

cases.reason: Management arming/release and CDP must be inaccessible even though data-plane HTTP is live.
requiredActualObservations: Requests through the public HTTP origin cannot change private management state or retrieve CDP data.
Private controller sequence remains unchanged and authenticated/local private management positive control still succeeds. No topology control URL is served by the subject app.

cases.reason: Admission must inspect actual native restrictions rather than infer them from network names or declared flags.
requiredActualObservations: Each forbidden actual configuration is rejected before the literal app starts.
Retain rejected native configuration and owned setup cleanup. A synthetic configuration object alone is unit coverage, not native isolation evidence.

cases.reason: Opaque invalid UTF-8 and binary bytes must survive without text decoding, compression or newline rewriting.
requiredActualObservations: Upstream raw request and downstream raw response equal the literal full HTTP/1.1 byte streams exactly.
Body bytes, lengths and SHA256 match separately. No replacement-character decoding, reserialization, automatic content encoding or extra bytes.

cases.reason: A bounded raw HTTP/1.1 proxy must preserve chunk framing, extensions, trailers and cross-chunk code points.
requiredActualObservations: Both raw full wire streams match exactly, including chunk extensions, CRLF boundaries, terminal zero chunk and literal trailer.
Decoded entity bytes also match independently; preserving only text/entity bytes cannot satisfy the raw-wire predicate.
This freezes HTTP/1.1 byte-forwarding semantics for the literal infrastructure. HTTP/2 translation/rechunking is outside this inventory and cannot be silently substituted.

cases.reason: Full duplex means the proxy does not wait for complete request buffering before forwarding a response.
requiredActualObservations: Native socket observations establish each causal barrier in order using explicit private acknowledgments, not cross-process wall clocks.
Exact final request ABCDEFGH and response 12345678 complete once; neither direction is silently drained or ended.

cases.reason: Backpressure requires observed producer suspension/drain while preserving every byte, not a small successful buffered transfer.

literalStimulus.bodyGenerator: bytes 0x00 through 0xff, in that order, repeated 256 times

requiredActualObservations: Run each direction separately with the receiving peer held at a private barrier. Observe a native producer write returning false, then drain/resumption after the private release.
Complete bytes/hash match the literal 65536-byte sequence and per-proxy queued-byte counters remain within frozen bounds.
If this bounded setup does not induce observable backpressure, mark the capability NOT_MEASURED/BLOCKED; do not call a buffered transfer a positive backpressure result.

cases.reason: Next action CSRF/origin behavior must not be silently repaired by the intermediary.
requiredActualObservations: Upstream fixture observes exact frozen Host, Origin and supplied forwarded-header bytes; the intermediary injects no trusted origin assertion or action identity.
Controller correlation does not trust these client-provided strings. Real Next stable-origin/forwarded-origin compatibility remains unmeasured and requires separate source review.

cases.reason: Exactly one private handshake must hold and later forward exactly one eligible request.

handshake: release ARM-0001/REQ-0001 acknowledged at control ordinal 3

requiredActualObservations: Before release the client request is pending and the upstream fixture has received zero request bytes.
After release upstream receives exactly one full unchanged request, emits literal ACK-A-01 once, and client observes complete native response once.
Retained cross-references bind each private acknowledgment to native connection/request observations. ARM-0001 or a nonce alone provides no action authenticity.

cases.reason: Unrelated routes must continue while the exact request is held.
requiredActualObservations: Other response completes before releasing held save; held request has no upstream bytes and no manufactured response terminal.
This is finite literal behavior only; actual Next same-route action/navigation queueing remains unknown.

cases.reason: Same-route concurrency is ambiguous and cannot be resolved by first-match timing.
requiredActualObservations: Controller marks the armed case AMBIGUOUS/BLOCKED; it does not select either request as authentic.
No successful release/effect receipt is emitted. Any sockets closed during safe cleanup retain their abort outcomes, never successful EOF.

cases.reason: Repeated or wrong releases cannot forward a request twice or invent a second acknowledgment.
requiredActualObservations: Wrong identifiers fail without forwarding. The one correct release forwards once; a duplicate release is explicitly rejected and the case is not fully complete.
Upstream full-request count stays one and there is only one native response.

cases.reason: Missing state/correlation must fail closed without guessing from clocks or untrusted success output.
requiredActualObservations: Each missing/contradictory state produces an explicit BLOCKED infrastructure result.
No ordinary response, clock coincidence, route match, arbitrary nonce or stdout status supplies the absent private handshake edge.

cases.reason: Client abort during a partially forwarded request must reach upstream rather than become a complete request.
requiredActualObservations: Upstream sees exactly the four-byte prefix then native close/error with incomplete message; no EOF/success/ACK is manufactured.
Controller aborts the paired upstream socket, retains both outcomes and does not drain remaining client bytes or retry the request.

cases.reason: Upstream abort after a partial response must reach the client without manufactured loadingFinished.
requiredActualObservations: Client receives exact four-byte prefix then native incomplete/close/error, not a complete eight-byte response.
Controller propagates the abort, emits no replacement response, zero chunk, extra padding, retry or success; literal infrastructure outcome is expected BLOCKED.

cases.reason: A canceled held request cannot be forwarded after a late private release.
requiredActualObservations: Upstream receives zero bytes; late release is rejected as aborted.
Client/paired controller outcomes remain canceled/incomplete. Cleanup does not turn them into complete responses.

cases.reason: Upstream failure before headers must not be silently transformed into product success.

literalStimulus.upstreamAction: close accepted socket before response headers

requiredActualObservations: Client observes native failure/incomplete response; no synthetic HTTP 200 or EOF success is emitted.
Original error and controller/cleanup errors are retained separately. A proxy-generated diagnostic, if explicitly designed later, cannot qualify product transport completion.

cases.reason: Request and response byte limits must fail closed in either direction.

literalStimulus.overBodyGenerator: bytes 0x00 through 0xff repeated 256 times, followed by 0x5a

requiredActualObservations: Run request and response overflow separately. The one extra byte is detected without unbounded buffering and no successful complete forwarding/result is claimed.
Retain the complete bounded synthetic input and actual bytes seen at each peer, overflow ordinal, byte counts, raw error and aborted socket outcomes.

cases.reason: HTTP framing ambiguity/overlong headers cannot be normalized into an apparently exact request.
requiredActualObservations: Reject ambiguous/malformed framing or retain a native incomplete outcome, without forwarding a reinterpreted successful request.
No dropped header, guessed length, text conversion or synthesized terminating chunk hides the original bytes.

cases.reason: Every held socket and whole attempt must have a finite deadline with honest timeout evidence.

operations: upstream headers arrive but body never completes

requiredActualObservations: Actual deadline expires, the result is TIMEOUT/BLOCKED and every owned socket/container cleanup is attempted independently.

No partial output, retained heartbeat, HTTP 200 header or release-after-deadline creates completion. Actual elapsed/native signals are retained; synthetic clock tests alone are not native timeout evidence.

cases.reason: Correlation/event inventory is finite and append-only.
requiredActualObservations: Every condition produces BLOCKED with the original bounded sequence retained; no deduplication/relabeling discards contradictory evidence.
Replay of retained trusted infrastructure observations must agree with the initial assessment. This does not replace the frozen browser protocol/v1 reducer.

cases.reason: Full bounded nonempty raw process output must be retained as bytes, not only count/digest.
requiredActualObservations: Retained stdout/stderr byte files match exact literals, byte counts and independently recomputed SHA256.

Exit status, signal, timing, exact argv, native inspected configuration, role/image identity and artifact inventory accompany the raw files. Invalid UTF-8 stderr remains raw bytes; presentation decoding cannot replace it.

cases.reason: Missing/tampered native evidence cannot be interpreted as empty, default or current.

counterfactuals: nonzero exit hidden by PASS text

requiredActualObservations: Each exact deficiency is BLOCKED and named; no fallback to a boolean, historical receipt or digest-only absent raw stream.
Before/after closure and installed-byte inventory comparison must be explicit.

cases.reason: Automatic removal may make explicit rm fail; native exact-owned absence can still establish cleanup.
requiredActualObservations: Requires an explicitly successful native inventory query with an explicitly present empty byte stream and exact-owned selectors.
Native removal failure and successful absence query raw outputs/statuses are both retained. No claim about unrelated containers/resources.

cases.reason: Cleanup must not convert evidence absence or leftovers into success, nor hide a primary failure.

counterfactuals: one cleanup fails after primary abort

requiredActualObservations: Cleanup is BLOCKED for each missing or nonempty owned inventory. All other owned cleanup actions still run.
Retain primary abort/error and each cleanup error independently; preserve raw removal/list/config outputs.

cases.reason: Partial setup cleanup must be bounded to owned resources and leave no discoverable executable fixtures.

literalStimulus.abortStage: after network and scratch creation before app starts

requiredActualObservations: All and only actually created owned resources are removed with successful explicit absence queries.
Unrelated sentinel identity is unchanged; fresh owned scratch is gone and no .test.ts/.tsx fixture copies remain discoverable. Any retained source snapshot uses inert .txt/JSON.

qualification.positiveControls: A positive infrastructure case must produce the exact actual byte/native configuration/causal observations, complete raw evidence and verified owned cleanup.
qualification.negativeControls: A negative case passes only by demonstrating the expected infrastructure refusal/abort/blocking behavior with honest native observations. It does not make a failing product/native journey acceptable.
qualification.missingOrUnavailable: No native capability/setup, uninduced backpressure, absent listener positive control, missing correlation or cleanup observation is UNKNOWN/BLOCKED, not a passing negative test.
qualification.testOwnership: A future implementation owner cannot alter these expected observations from observed output. Source-backed prospective amendments retain original inventory/hash and reason; all baseline failures remain preserved.

missingNativeCapabilitiesAndDependencies: No implementation or execution of this literal topology exists from this document; network/policy mechanisms, private management transport and exact socket observation adapter require independent review.
Literal DB/CDP endpoints do not test actual Postgres roles/schema/TLS, synthetic app auth, Chromium/CDP behavior or browser-origin security.
Real Next production build/dependencies/fonts/platform/image closure and resource capacity are unmeasured; no capacity follows from these small byte cases.

Next Server Action queuing, stable browser origin, request-hold behavior and exact browser/intermediary/app/DB association remain unmeasured. Do not derive action authority from public labels/nonces or raw server-reference manifests.
Strict v1 request cancellation/missing-EOF causes remain unresolved. This inventory does not add a waiver, change the 100 component predicates or satisfy either required native group.
